headline: Imposed one-year demolition delay on 63 Greenwood Lane; found 893-897 Main Street not preferably preserved.
summary: Commissioners held demolition delay hearings for 63 Greenwood Lane and for 893-897 Main Street and 6-8 Hammond Street. A motion to find 63 Greenwood Lane not preferably preserved did not carry, so a one-year demolition delay was imposed. The building at 893-897 Main Street and 6-8 Hammond Street was found not preferably preserved, and spending up to $1000 was authorized for reprinting brochures.
decisions: Motion to find 63 Greenwood Lane NOT preferably preserved failed, 2-3; a one-year demolition delay was imposed.
Authorized Commissioner Isaacson to contact the Waltham Law Department about the timeline questions raised by Richard LeClair on 63 Greenwood Lane.
Found 893-897 Main Street and 6-8 Hammond Street NOT preferably preserved, 5-0.
Authorized spending up to $1000 on reprinting the Waltham Watch Factory area history brochures, 5-0.
Authorized Commissioner Isaacson to send a letter opposing proposed Section 106 review changes on behalf of the commission, 5-0.

4.   Chair: Announcements: 
 
A demolition application was submitted for 245 Beal Road. It was found not historically 
significant, so did not require a public hearing.   
 
 
Chair: Reading and Description of Correspondence: 
 
Commissioner Isaacson was contacted by the Waltham Times about the proposed changes to 
the Section 106 review process and was interviewed for an article.  
  
    
5.   Chair: Public Hearings: 
 
Demolition Delay Hearings: 
 
63 Greenwood Lane 
 
Richard LeClair represented the house, which he said was not structurally sound. There were 
several additions to the original house, which is located in the historic Piety Corner 
neighborhood. A history of the house was read by Commissioner Dufromont.  The house sits 
next to a stone wall that marks a colonial lot line from 1636. The house was owned by 
several very prominent Waltham residents from the time it was built by the Worcester family 
around 1886. Commissioner Isaacson felt that the house was historically significant. 
Commissioners Egirous and Dufromont questioned the structural integrity of the house. The 
current owners did not have plans to present for a new structure. Gary Rogers, a member of 
the public, gave his input. He said he toured the house to explore the possibility of renovating 
it but felt that it would be too expensive to preserve. John Morrison, a member of the public 
who grew up in the house, gave his input. He shared his fondness for the house and said he 
would hate to see it be demolished.  
 
Commissioner Egirous moved to find the house NOT preferably preserved. 
Commissioner Dufromont seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, no 
      Commissioner Daly, absent 
      Commissioner Dufromont, no 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent
Page 3 of 6 
 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
            Commissioner Wilson, no 
 
      The motion did not carry and a one year demolition delay was imposed. 
 
Richard LeClair questioned the timeline of the response and hearing because the application 
was submitted in April and the ordinance says the hearing should be held within 30 days. He 
requested that the delayed demolition time clock begin in April, when the application was 
submitted. Commissioner Isaacson said that the issue was with the Building Department not 
forwarding the application to the Historical Commission in a timely manner, not that the 
Historical Commission didn’t follow the timeline outlined for them in the ordinance. 
Commissioner Isaacson felt that Mr. LeClair’s questions should be referred to the Waltham 
Law Department. 
 
Commissioner Wilson moved to authorize Commissioner Isaacson to contact the 
Waltham Law Department about this matter. 
Commissioner Russo seconded. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
      Commissioner Isaacson, yes 
      Commissioner Daly, absent 
      Commissioner Dufromont, yes 
      Commissioner Egirous, yes 
      Commissioner Migdal, absent 
      Commissioner Russo, yes 
            Commissioner Wilson, yes 
 
 
893-897 Main Street and 6-8 Hammond Street 
 
Bret Francis represented the property. A history of the building was read by Commissioner 
Dufromont.  Commissioner Isaacson gave a brief history of the area around the building. The 
building at 893-897 Main Street was built between 1890 and 1891. Businesses in the building 
included a bakery, hardware store, grocery store, and restaurants, over the years. The 
residences above were not connected with the businesses. The building had several owners 
throughout its history, including a member of the Lawrence family who built the Lawrence 
Block at Main and Common Streets. It is one of the earliest commercial buildings on the 
west end of Main Street. Mr. Francis pointed out that the building has been vacant since a 
fire there in 2025 caused extensive damage. He also summarized the plan for future 
development of commercial spaces and residential units above, with parking. 
 
Commissioner Dufromont moved to find the building NOT preferably preserved. 
Commissioner Wilson seconded.

10. Old Business:  
 
Officer elections could not happen until all commissioners were present at a meeting. 
 
 
11. New Business:  
 
The National Trust for Historic Preservation outlined proposed changes by the federal 
government to the Section 106 review process, which allows local review of any changes or 
renovations to federally owned properties, such as local post office branch buildings or cell 
tower antenna installations. The proposed changes would eliminate notification and reviews 
by local historical commissions. Commissioner Isaacson suggested that the commissioners 
authorize him to send a letter on behalf of the Historical Commission when the public 
comment period begins and said that commissioners could also send their own comment 
letters individually. 
 
Commissioner Wilson moved to authorize Commissioner Isaacson to send a letter 
opposing these changes on behalf of the Waltham Historical Commission. 
Commissioner Russo seconded.
